note: V4 and V5 subjects. The target is the V2 crop (bench/v2/targets/). The painter paints it at source scale: width is the crop's own width in pixels, one sheet cell for each crop pixel, and sheetmm is that width at 0.259 mm a cell (mmPerCell in bench/v2/crops.json), so a crop is a detail about 78 mm wide and is never enlarged. A subject wider than its target stops the painter (tools/plate/source-scale.mjs) and fails bench/scripts/subjects.test.mjs. Until 0.3.3 the subjects were painted 1200 to 1224 px wide on sheets of 158 and 280 mm, four times the crop; the published V096 results were painted that way. medium: the drawing medium a person sees in the target itself: pen (pen-and-ink lines), pencil (faint graphite lines under the paint, no pen) or none (no drawn line). On a subject whose medium is not pen, a plan's ink drawing is drawn in graphite before the washes (bench/scripts/pipeline/plan-args.mjs subjectMediumRule). Trumbull is none: its darks (window bars, stone joints, the sign) change colour and width from mark to mark as brushed paint does, there is no even pen line, and no pencil line shows through the washes. Mittens is pencil: the whiskers and hair ends are thin grey lines, lighter than any pen. Sargent and the painted dog show no drawn line.
